notes:
Top-line: RapidLoop builds an IDE-native copilot for enterprise dev teams (VS Code + internal web IDE). Evaluating Redwood for low-latency streaming + token-budget controls to hit dev UX SLAs.

What they care about:
- TTFT targets: median ~80ms, p95 <200ms for single-line completion streaming (very sensitive to first-token latency).
- Jitter: want <20ms stdev (per-session) to avoid flaky typing experience; spikes >100ms seen in current provider unacceptable.
- Backpressure: on noisy/high-concurrency sessions they need graceful degradation (shorter completions, fall back to local cached suggestions) rather than total timeouts.
- Token budget tuning: per-seat/month budget + per-session micro-budgets; ability to set soft caps and automatic truncation strategies.
- Model/version pinning: must pin to specific quantized model variant for deterministic latency; want automated fallbacks to smaller quantized model on overload.

Quote from CTO: "If TTFT is >100ms our editor loses the feel of instant completion — we will lose adoption. We need predictable first-byte behavior and a clear billing model for token bursts."

POC ask: 2-week dedicated capacity trial (50 concurrent dev seats), telemetry hooks for TTFT, jitter histograms, and an autopilot policy for budget exhaustion (soft cap -> shorter responses -> unblock). Want integration points: VS Code extension SDK hooks + websocket streaming.

Docs shared: latency spec (drive link), current SDK/extension repo (private), cost model spreadsheet. Security: require SSO/SAML + audit logs + KMS for keys.

Sales notes: price sensitivity around per-seat burst billing vs flat seat fee. Favoring Redwood Dedicated if latency SLOs validated. AE to push POC SOW and finalize ATO checklist for VPC connection.
